Title: PowerShell Command Injection in Generated Completion Script via Invoke-Expression
Analysis:
In powershell_completions.go, the generated PowerShell completion script uses `Invoke-Expression` to run `$RequestComp`, which is constructed from the command elements input by the user during command line interaction/completion (specifically `$CommandAst.CommandElements`).
Since `$Command` is built directly from the untrusted command arguments typed in PowerShell, if a user types a command with shell metacharacters or payloads in the argument, those elements are split into `$Program` and `$Arguments` and executed via `Invoke-Expression`.
This results in arbitrary PowerShell Command Injection / Code Execution in the context of the user's PowerShell session when completing commands.

Source: $CommandAst.CommandElements (the user's command line input to trigger tab completion)
Sanitization: None
Sink: Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To trigger arbitrary command execution when tab-completing a cobra-based tool (e.g. `mycmd`):
Type: `mycmd ; Start-Process calc ;` then press TAB.
This constructs a Command string which is executed by Invoke-Expression, triggering the injection payload (e.g., launching calculator).
Snippet:
#call the command store the output in $out and redirect stderr and stdout to null
    # $Out is an array contains each line per element
    Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null
